title: Pig identification requirements in the UK
subtitle: What the law requires before pigs move off your holding.
excerpt: Every pig in the UK must be identified before it leaves the holding where it was born. The method and timing depend on whether the pig is going to slaughter, to another holding, or to a show. The rules are set under the Livestock (Identification and Registration) legislation and enforced by the AHDB. Here is what you need to know for a small holding keeping pigs for the first time.
sourceNotes: DEFRA, Guidance on pig identification (2023). AHDB Pork, Pig Identification Requirements factsheet. Food Standards Agency, traceability in pigs.

glossaryTerms.definition: A temporary identification mark applied to the shoulder of a pig using a slapmark ink and a mechanical stamping device. Required before pigs move to slaughter. Shows the herd mark (county code + individual number) of the farm of origin.
A unique identifier assigned to a pig-keeping holding by the local authority. Consists of a two-letter county code followed by a four-digit number. Required on all pig identification marks.

content.text: Any holding keeping pigs in the UK must register with the local authority and obtain a

before any pig can leave the holding. This applies even for a single pet pig moved to a vet or to slaughter. Registration is free and completed online through the government's livestock registration service.
Pigs going directly from your holding to a slaughterhouse must be marked with a

on both shoulders immediately before loading. The slap mark uses your herd mark. Slapmark sets (ink, stamp, and applicator) are available from agricultural merchants. The tattoo ink must be food-safe.

Pigs moved to another holding (not slaughter) must be permanently identified before leaving. Current accepted methods are ear tags, ear tattoos, and electronic identification (EID). Tags must show the herd mark. Guidance on approved tag types and placement positions is published on the government's website. Permanent ear tags are mandatory for pigs going to other farms, shows, or markets.

Every movement of pigs off your holding (to slaughter, to another farm, to a show) requires a movement licence (eAML2 in England and Wales) issued before the pigs leave. This is completed online through the eAML2 system and prints a paper version the driver takes with the animals.
A standstill period of 20 days applies after pigs arrive on a holding: no other pigs may move off that holding for 20 days (unless going directly to slaughter). Plan movements accordingly.
A holding register (medicine book and movement record) must be maintained and kept for at least 3 years.
